title: Salah, Wudu and Niyya: IB Islam Study Guide
summary: Salah wudu niyya explained for IB World Religions SL, with Quran references, Sunni and Shia interpretations, key terms, themes and exam analysis.
body_markdown:
Salah, wudu and niyya are connected stages of Islamic worship. **Salah** is formal ritual prayer, **wudu** is the minor ritual purification commonly performed before it, and **niyya** is the intention that gives the action its religious purpose. Together, they show that worship in Islam involves the body, mind and will.


For IB World Religions SL, knowing the sequence is only the beginning. Strong analysis asks what these practices communicate about submission to Allah, responsibility, community and the relationship between outward action and inward commitment.


### Salah, wudu and niyya at a glance


Key term Arabic Essential meaning IB significance


Salah ṣalāh Formal ritual prayer performed at prescribed times Connects ritual, belief, ethics and religious experience


Wudu wuḍūʾ Minor ritual purification using water Shows physical preparation for a sacred act


Niyya niyyah Intention or conscious purpose Connects visible practice with inward sincerity


Qibla qiblah Direction of the Kaaba in Mecca Gives geographically dispersed worshippers a shared orientation


Rak'ah rakʿah One cycle of prayer movements and recitations Unites words, posture and disciplined repetition


Khushu khushūʿ Reverent attentiveness and humility Highlights the intended inner quality of prayer


A useful revision checklist is:


- Define each Arabic term precisely.
- Explain how wudu and niyya prepare a Muslim for salah.
- Support analysis with the Quran and hadith.
- Compare Sunni and Shia interpretations while connecting the practices to the fundamental questions and course themes.


RevisionDojo's[notes on shahadah, salah and zakat](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-world-religions/ib-world-religions-522-the-pillars-i-shahadah-salah-and-zakat/notes) provide a useful foundation for placing prayer within the Five Pillars.


### What is salah?


Salah is the formal act of Islamic prayer and one of the Five Pillars. Muslims perform five obligatory prayers each day: **Fajr** , **Dhuhr** , **Asr** , **Maghrib** and **Isha** .


The Quran describes prayer as prescribed at specified times in Surah 4:103. In Surah 20:14, Allah commands prayer for divine remembrance. Salah is therefore an ordered response to God, repeated even without spontaneous inspiration.


A prayer consists of units called **rak'at** , the plural of rak'ah. These contain recitation, standing ( **qiyam** ), bowing ( **ruku** ) and prostration ( **sujud** ). The worshipper faces the qibla and recites passages including Surah al-Fatihah. Prostration makes submission an embodied action rather than an abstract idea.


This distinction matters in an IB answer. **Du'a** is personal supplication and may be expressed more freely. Salah has prescribed times, words and movements. Both can be called prayer in English, but they should not be treated as identical. RevisionDojo's[guide to prayer, fasting, du'a and Hajj](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-world-religions/ib-world-religions-551-group-and-individual-experience-prayer-fasting-93214/notes) helps clarify the relationship between communal forms and personal religious experience.


### Why wudu comes before prayer


Wudu is a form of ritual purification normally required before salah when a person's state of wudu has been broken. Surah 5:6 directs believers to wash the face and arms, wipe the head and attend to the feet. It also provides for purification with clean earth when water is unavailable or unsuitable, known as **tayammum** .


Wudu should not be reduced to hygiene. Its religious meaning concerns **taharah** , or ritual purity. Someone can be physically clean yet still need wudu before prayer. Completing the external motions without the relevant intention also raises questions about whether the action counts as worship.


### Niyya and the meaning behind the action


Niyya is the intention to perform an act for its religious purpose. Before salah, a worshipper knows which prayer is being offered and directs it toward Allah. Niyya is generally an inward orientation rather than a required spoken formula.


The often-cited hadith opening Sahih al-Bukhari states that deeds are judged according to intentions. Two outwardly similar actions can therefore have different religious meanings. Washing to cool down is not automatically wudu, and bowing to retrieve an object is not ruku within salah.


This avoids a simplistic contrast between ritual and sincerity. Niyya directs the form, while the form trains and expresses the intention.


Two students compare a towering stack of memorized definitions with a blank answer sheet requiring conceptual connections.


Definitions matter, but IB analysis must explain how the concepts depend on one another.


### Sunni and Shia interpretations


Sunni and Shia Muslims affirm prayer, purification and intention, although their jurisprudential traditions differ over some details.


### Wudu and the feet


In the major Sunni legal traditions, the feet are washed during wudu. In Twelver Shia jurisprudence, the upper surfaces of the feet are wiped with moisture remaining from the ablution. The difference reflects grammatical and interpretive readings of Quran 5:6, supported by each tradition's legal authorities.


Differences also exist within Sunni Islam. The Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali schools do not classify every element of wudu identically. Intention is obligatory in several schools, while Hanafi jurisprudence generally treats it as strongly recommended rather than a condition of validity.


### Prayer times and movements


Sunni and Twelver Shia Muslims recognize five obligatory daily prayers. Twelver Shia practice permits Dhuhr with Asr and Maghrib with Isha to be performed consecutively within broader periods. Sunni traditions also permit combining prayers in specified circumstances, such as travel, although the rules vary by legal school.


Other variations include hand position and the surface used for prostration. Many Twelver Shia worshippers place the forehead on natural earth or another permissible natural material, often called a **turbah** . Worship is directed to Allah, not the material. That distinction demonstrates factual knowledge and respectful interpretation.


### The three fundamental questions


IB World Religions organizes comparison around three fundamental questions. Salah, wudu and niyya can address each one.


### What is the human condition?


Human beings are capable of remembering Allah but also of distraction, forgetfulness and wrongdoing. Regular prayer acknowledges dependence on God and the need to redirect attention. Wudu represents preparation, while niyya recognizes responsibility for both movements and purpose.


### Where are we going?


Islam teaches accountability before Allah and an afterlife in which human actions matter. Salah places everyday life within that larger horizon. Each interruption of work, study or rest suggests that immediate concerns are not the final measure of existence.


### How do we get there?


The Islamic answer includes faith, divine guidance, worship, repentance and ethical conduct. Salah provides a repeated path of remembrance and submission. Quran 29:45 associates genuine prayer with restraint from indecency and wrongdoing, connecting worship to moral formation rather than treating it as an isolated ceremony.


### Connecting salah to the five themes


IB theme Connection to salah, wudu and niyya


Rituals Prescribed prayer uses repeated times, movements, recitations and purification practices


Sacred texts Quran 5:6, 4:103, 20:14 and 29:45 provide important textual foundations, while hadith informs practice


Doctrines and beliefs Worship expresses tawhid, revelation, human accountability and submission to Allah


Religious experience Salah may cultivate humility, attentiveness and belonging, individually and in congregation


Ethics and moral conduct Prayer is associated with disciplined conduct, responsibility and resistance to wrongdoing


The themes overlap. A ritual draws authority from sacred texts, expresses doctrines, shapes experience and may influence ethical conduct. Strong examination paragraphs follow those connections instead of discussing each theme in isolation. RevisionDojo's[overview of public and private worship](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-world-religions/ib-world-religions-322-public-and-private-worship-eucharist-prayer-an-93132) offers another useful comparative lens.


### How to turn knowledge into IB analysis


A focused paragraph can begin with a claim: “Wudu shows that preparation for worship is both external and intentional.” It can then use Quran 5:6 as evidence, explain taharah, introduce niyya and compare Sunni washing with Twelver Shia wiping of the feet. The final sentence should return to significance, perhaps arguing that shared submission can coexist with jurisprudential diversity.


Avoid merely listing prayer movements. Instead, ask what each element communicates. Facing one qibla can express the unity of the **ummah** , the worldwide Muslim community. Prostration can communicate humility. Congregational prayer can turn an individual obligation into a social experience. The[Islam in context study notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-world-religions/ib-world-religions-171-islam-in-context-the-prophet-the-quran-and-the-ummah/notes) can help you connect worship to the Quran, Prophet Muhammad and ummah.


For revision, combine concise Study Notes and Flashcards with application. Use RevisionDojo's Questionbank to practise explanation and comparison, then use AI Chat and Grading tools to identify unsupported generalizations. Predicted Papers and Mock Exams can develop timing, while the Coursework Library and Tutors support deeper investigation. The[World Religions misconceptions guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-world-religions-misconceptions) is especially useful for checking oversimplified claims, and the[investigative study requirements](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-world-religions/ib-world-religions-811-what-the-investigative-study-is-requirements-at-a-glance/notes) show how an interest in prayer can become a focused inquiry.


Salah is structured, but it is not empty structure. Wudu prepares the worshipper, niyya directs the act, and prayer joins remembrance to disciplined action. Once those relationships become clear, Islam key concepts stop looking like separate definitions. They become a coherent account of how belief is practised, experienced and carried into ethical life. That connected understanding is what RevisionDojo helps IB World Religions students build.
